abstract.t: This document defines a tenant lifecycle profile for S/MIME deployments operating under CNSA 2.0 algorithm requirements. It specifies how a multi-tenant S/MIME environment manages per-tenant trust stores, certificate issuance and rotation, and algorithm compliance across the certificate lifecycle, ensuring that CNSA 2.0 constraints are enforced consistently for each tenant's messaging security configuration.

section.name: Introduction
section.t: S/MIME provides message-level security for email and is widely deployed in environments subject to CNSA 2.0. In a multi-tenant messaging environment (e.g., a hosted email provider serving multiple organizations), each tenant has distinct trust stores, certificate authorities, and algorithm policies. This document defines a lifecycle profile that governs per-tenant S/MIME configuration under CNSA 2.0, from certificate issuance through rotation and retirement.
This section will describe the multi-tenant S/MIME context and the lifecycle management challenge under CNSA 2.0.

section.name: Conventions and Definitions
section.t: The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "NOT RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" in this document are to be interpreted as described in BCP 14 when, and only when, they appear in all capitals as shown here.

section.name: Per-Tenant Trust Stores
section.t: This section will define the structure and management of per-tenant S/MIME trust stores: how each tenant's set of trusted certificate authorities and trusted public keys is isolated, how CNSA 2.0 algorithm requirements constrain the accepted certificates in a tenant's trust store, and how trust-store updates are versioned and audited.

section.name: Certificate Issuance and Rotation
section.t: This section will specify the certificate lifecycle under CNSA 2.0: issuance requirements (the certificate signature algorithm must be CNSA 2.0-approved), rotation procedures (how a new certificate supersedes an expiring one without message-decryption gaps), and retirement (how expired or revoked certificates are removed from the trust store while preserving the ability to decrypt historical messages).

section.name: Algorithm Compliance Enforcement
section.t: This section will define how CNSA 2.0 algorithm requirements are enforced across the lifecycle: which signature and key-encapsulation algorithms are permitted for new issuance, how the transition dates in CNSA 2.0 map to lifecycle enforcement actions, and how non-compliant certificates are flagged for rotation.

section.name: Security Considerations
section.t: This section will address threats to the tenant lifecycle: cross-tenant trust-store contamination, stale certificate acceptance, key-escrow and decryption-history requirements, and the integrity of the rotation procedure.
